text: For more than a decade, the government had tried to force the Chiricahua Apache onto the San Carlos reservation, far to the north. Many refused. Small bands broke away again and again — the most famous led by a Bedonkohe warrior named Geronimo.
But the story of how the Chiricahua lost these mountains began twenty-five years earlier — with a misunderstanding inside an Army tent.
The peace Cochise made did not outlive him for long. Within twelve years, his people were on those trains heading east. But the mountains he defended are far older than any war — and far stranger.

And from the top of the park, on the horizon to the north, the mountains form a shape that many visitors see as a giant face lying on its back, looking at the sky. Look for the forehead, the nose and the chin. It's called Cochise Head.
But the rocks are only part of what makes these mountains rare. Some of what lives here was only caught on camera a few years ago.
